note: Turks and Caicos Islands is a British Overseas Territory (British Nationality Act 1981, Schedule 6). Its people's nationality is British overseas territories citizenship, and those who held it in 2002 became British citizens too (British Overseas Territories Act 2002, s. 3). So the United Kingdom's rules on naturalisation and on keeping citizenship are modelled as theirs; the territory's own belonger or status rules, and its own passport, are the passports engine's.

sources.title: legislation.gov.uk, British Overseas Territories Act 2002, section 3 (Conferral on British overseas territories citizens)
sources.said: Any person who, immediately before the commencement of this section, is a British overseas territories citizen shall, on the commencement of this section, become a British citizen. (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a person who is a British overseas territories citizen by virtue only of a connection with the Sovereign Base Areas of Akrotiri and Dhekelia.
